title: One of the twelve border motifs has the wrong curve
her_words: i need these bump in clean curves, dont exaggerate, stick to the first reference image. do this for both sides of the rug in this portion. make sure all the curves are uniform
source: transcripts/md/8d5c6092-6fd2-4a55-a612-5d30ed09ed32.md:8078 (also :8830 "i want the curves next to the red portion also to be uniform", :10148 "uniform clean curves, no exaggeration, strictly follow the reference for the curves"); catalogue P2, P6
context: A 1800 x 560 px rug border: twelve taupe protrusions in a row, each in its own group, the right six inside a second group that is flipped. The ninth motif from the left is taller, lumpier and leans, the other eleven are identical. A pink band hides the bottom of motifs 3 to 5, and a thin line runs across all of them.
requirement: Make the ninth motif's outline match the other eleven (same height, same lobes, no lean), by moving its existing points. Leave the other eleven exactly as they are.
references: any of the other eleven motifs 'Curve'
must_not_change: the long thin sage line drawn across the border
the inner maroon contour line inside each motif
the yellow and sage dots on each motif
the tiny diamonds and dots in the echo row above
acceptance: Motif 9 is the same shape and height as its neighbours, side by side
No other motif moved by even a pixel
Motif 9 is still where it was (same base, same centre) and mirrored correctly in the flipped half
The pink band, the sage line and the dots look the same as before
The hidden older copy under motif 9 is not what was edited
traps: The reference motif in the left half lives in unflipped local space and the target in a flipped one; copying coordinates without the group transform makes a mirror-image or displaced motif
Each motif sits in its own group with a translation, so local coordinates look identical across motifs while the spread coordinates do not
A hidden old version of motif 9 sits under it with the right shape; it must not be edited or revealed, and it must not be mistaken for a perfect reference
The pink band covers the base of motifs 3 to 5, so a render-based match on those would be wrong
The thin sage line and the inner contour lie over the motifs and share their colour with other shapes in a colour filter
Tiny 6 to 14 px diamonds and dots are close by
expected_reason: Clear, reversible and node-only. The off motif has the same point count as the others, so fit_to_reference works once it handles the group transforms.
